At Little Waves, summertime means thirst-quenching iced pouroversand this one is truly something special. Were spotlighting Mauricio Shattahs Competition Series Typica Mejorado from Colombia. Its vibrant, balanced, and absolutely shines over ice.

 Mauricio ferments this coffee for 48 hours in stainless steel tanks using carefully selected yeasts, creating a clean, vibrant profile.

 He also uses nitrogen to flush out CO during fermentation, preventing the buildup of carbonic acid. The result is an ultra-smooth cup without any sharpness.

 The cherries are dried slowly over 68 weeks in rooms that filter out UV light, allowing only soft infrared rays. 

This slow, gentle process produces a cup that stays floral and beautifully balancedeven when chilled.

We brewed it with an Origami Air S and Sibarist Small Cone filter, ground at #11.5 on our EK43 Mahlknig, using 196F water. In the cup? Refreshing notes of peach and mango.

 Want to brew it yourself? Check out our iced pourover recipe and experience this standout coffee (or your favorite Little Waves) over ice.

Where The Rain Sleeps is a washed coffee from Kenya  

Established in 1998, Gondo coffee factory currently has 727 producers in the Kihoya subregion Muranga countys Mathioya District. 

After carefully tending their coffee trees all season, Gondos producers selectively hand-pick ripe red cherries as they reach perfection. Even with all that care, they give a second post-harvest pass, separating ripe cherry from underripes, overripes, and any foreign matter that makes it into the mix.

Giving bright fruitiness, the 16-18 hour fermentation process in cement tanks produces a grapefruit, blackberry, jasmine, and effervescent cup.  

A nod to the cloud-covered Aberdare Mountain Range and the quiet majesty of the highlands, it is truly delicate, sweet, floral, poetic, and delicious!

These waves are the root origin of the words little waves that were part of Areli and me falling in love in 2010. 

Serene, calming cadence in touch with a deeper sense of tuneleads the mind to the ocean, the moon, and marvels, music, and patterns of the universe. 

When we bought our home in 2014 it became the name of our WiFi network. 

Later it became the name of our coffee roasting company @littlewaves.coffee  L

Weve purchased a few coffees from JNP Coffee founder Jeanine Niyonzima-Aroian because the quality is always superior.

In addition to her quality prerogatives, Jeanine also focuses specifically on increasing gender diversity within the Burundian coffee community. Jeanine is also the only woman majority shareholder of a larger Burundi coffee conglomerate and a role model not just in Burundi but also in the coffee community.

JNP works with organizations that focus on gender diversity and inclusivity in the region, such as the International Womens Coffee Alliance Burundi Chapter. They also founded the nonprofit Burundi Friends International to educate youth, improve financial literacy, and create self-sustaining communities.

As for Akeza, it means "beautiful" in Kirundi and this coffee represents Akeza very well. This coffee is bursting with sweetness, we loved it right off the bat. Akeza is grown in a notably remote area of Kayanza Province. Jeanine's first visit was not ideal, it was pouring rain and the roads were steep. At one point her team got out of their rented 4x4 truck to help some local farmers push it up the slope, but the truck kept sliding backwards. She felt certain that they were never going to get out! In that moment, she promised herself she was never coming back. And yet, after meeting the farmers and tasting the coffees, she realized that sometimes the most difficult places to get to are the best.

We've got another delicious coffee from Ana Donneys! With tasting notes of pink starburst, rum punch, and tamarind aftertaste, we are so excited to be sharing Azafrn Natural Caturra with y'all!

Straight from Ana Donneys herself (and translated)- "This coffee is very, very important to me. Azafrn Natural is one of Caf Primitivo's most representative coffees, not only for its sensorial profile, but also for the emotional and technical concept that underpins it. Its name is a tribute to my grandmother, a fundamental woman in our family history and a coffee lover, whose favorite flower was saffron. Inspired by its sweetness, elegance, and presence, we developed this coffee with the aim of capturing that same essence in every cup.

This process is characterized by a fruity, sweet, and complex cup, with notes of blueberries, juicy acidity, creamy body, and a balanced and lingering aftertaste. It is a vibrant, aromatic coffee with great structure and a clean, long finish.

The process begins in the field, with a highly selective harvest of cherries at their peak ripeness. This is followed by a 12-hour controlled oxidation, followed by a 72-hour fruit fermentation in hermetically sealed tanks designed to promote the development of volatile compounds responsible for aroma and tactile attributes such as acidity and body.

The coffee is slowly sun-dried on African beds to preserve the bean's lipid content. This component is essential to ensuring a cup with greater aromatic expression and stability over time, especially after roasting.
Each stage of the process is designed to guarantee homogeneity and sensorial expression, allowing the concept of this coffeea blend of family tradition, innovation, and the pursuit of excellenceto translate into a memorable cup experience."

Juneteenth (June 19th) is the longest-running Black holiday in the U.S.- signifying the continuous fight for freedom for all. On June 19, 1865, a union commander shared the news of the Emancipation Proclamation in Galveston, Texas- just one of the many places of the confederacy that continued instilling slavery two years after the Emancipation Proclamation was instilled in 1863. 

"The post-emancipation period known as Reconstruction (1865-1877) marked an era of great hope, uncertainty, and struggle for the nation as a whole. Formerly enslaved people immediately sought to reunify families, establish schools, run for political office, push radical legislation and even sue slaveholders for compensation. Given the 200+ years of enslavement, such changes were nothing short of amazing. Not even a generation out of slavery, African Americans were inspired and empowered to transform their lives and their country." - National Museum of African American History & Culture, Smithsonian.

Royal 7 is inspired by and in honor of Mary Elizabeth Clyburn, Rev. Douglas Elaine Moore, Claude Edward Glenn, Jesse Willard Gray, Vivian Elaine Jones, Melvin Haywood Willis, and Virginia Lee Williams, the seven young activists that led the first sit-in in North Carolina at Durham's Royal Ice Cream Parlor in protest of segregation and Jim Crow Laws. Though these are now moments of history, we still feel their presence and with the strength of the past, we can power the future.

We're so excited to be working with Benchmark Coffee Traders, who distribute high-quality green coffees from Sigri Estate in Papua New Guinea.

They have direct family ties with these coffee producers and work closely with them to bring their beautiful coffees to roasters in the U.S. 

Beyond producing a quality product, Benchmark Coffee Traders support a strong social agenda that provides free housing, free healthcare, and free schooling to the coffee pickers and farmers who work tirelessly to help produce these unique coffees.

Sigri Estate coffee is grown at over 5000 feet elevation. The estate considers soil and water conservation as a priority and is bird and eco-friendly, providing a habitat for more than 90 species of birds.

Sigri Estate Kula Peaberry specifically is a washed Arabica coffee that has undergone a rigorous wet factory process. Quality control begins in the field; cherries are hand-picked and carefully checked for uniformity, and then undergo a multi-step processing, grading, and sorting process. These specially processed "Kula" coffees are exclusive to our partners at Benchmark Coffee Traders, and the result is one of the cleanest PNG coffees being produced today.

We taste applesauce, pear, cinnamon, honey, and Brazil nut. Grab a bag of Sigri Estate Kula Peaberry to bring some Papua New Guinea to you.

Q.E.S. - Doi Pangkhon Natural comes to us from coffee producers in the Doi Pangkhon community in the Chiang Rai province of Thailand. The community includes around 300 households, each typically producing 12 tons of parchment coffee each year. @beanspirecoffee has worked in Doi Pangkhon, Chiang Rai for ten years, developing processing techniques, upgrading equipment, improving workflow, and working with producers individually to establish coffee cupping practices. All of the villagers in this producing area belong to Akha Hill Tribe and are notably young coffee farmers, ranging from 25-35 years of age. Beanspires co-founders, Fuadi Pitsuwan and Jane Kittiratanapaiboon, are part of the young generation moving the Thai coffee industry forward. Thailand is unique as a coffee-producing country; the countrys specialty cafe and roaster scene is thriving, and domestic consumption demands regularly outpace the countrys production volume. 

Only around 5% of Thailands specialty coffee is exported each year, while the rest is enjoyed by Thai coffee drinkers. This means that the coffees selected for export by the team at Beanspire are each chosen to share the work of Thai coffee producers with a global audience, providing a glimpse into the growing specialty coffee revolution happening in the country.

Coffea arabica started as one naturally occurring hybrid of two other species, Coffea eugenioides and Coffea canephora (commonly referred to as Robusta). This hybrid evolved over 100s of thousands of years, to the flavorful species that we drink today, in the shaded highlands of what we know today as SW Ethiopia and SE South Sudan.

That spontaneous event between two species was a polyploidal event that took place in what is now SW Ethiopia, NW Kenya, SE South Sudan. Unlike all other coffee species that have 22 chromosomes, Coffea arabica has 44. It has both stamens (seminal) and pistils (leading to the equivalent of ovaries) so a single flower has everything it needs to pollinate itself. Our guests opening the door and letting in the wind will pollinate the flowers.l, which only has a 48 hour window to take place before the flowers wither.

This is also one of the reasons that Arabica is so fragile and is currently slated to go extinct within 60 years. It has minimal genetic diversity on Earth as it pollinates itself and the great majority of coffee across the Earth lead back to two varieties that lead back to early cultivations in Yemen, Typica and Bourbon strains (which then developed on Reunion Island and became the Bourbon variety).

It is because of this fragility and impending extinction that Little Waves Coffee is a contributing member of @worldcoffeeresearch , a non profit that is doing much of the work to breed varieties, along with others who are preserving species with high cup quality and more climate resistance.

Ana Mara Donneys is a 5th generation coffee grower from Quindio, Colombia. She took over her family's coffee business after her grandfather passed away in 2019. She always heard how hard it was to produce coffee, so after selling her harvest for under the cost of production, she left to Bogota to look for a brighter future. There, she read about the opportunities that one could have if they focused on quality in coffee. @cafeprimitivo was started in 2020 to honor her family's legacy, especially her grandfather, Primitivo Correal Barrios and to focus on specialty coffee. 

Ana Mara is a Certified Q-Arabica Grader and the co-founder of IWCA Colombia, (International Women Coffee Alliance). IWCA Colombia offers a way of sharing knowledge and bringing people in all the coffee value chain together to create opportunities for women and young coffee producers in Colombia. Being a woman in charge of her farms doesn't come without its challenges but Ana has persevered and has surrounded herself with the people that will collectively do the work with mutual respect. She is committed to producing the best quality of specialty coffee, with certified agricultural, social and environmental practices.

What excites us about working with Ana is that she is a young visionary with an open heart and truly wants coffee to change the lives of those involved in getting the final product into your cup. She's involved with inspiring the next generation and always curious about how to continue to improve quality.

Worka Chelbessa comes from Gedeb, the most southern part of the Gedeo region, and the area is well known for producing incredible coffees. Yirgacheffe itself is famed for its beautifully delicate floral and citric coffees (think meyer lemon and bergamot, for example).

Neguesse Debela, the owner of the Ethiopian exporting company @snapspecialtycoffee , oversees two sites in the area and works with small producers as well. They produce spectacular washed coffees, and they continue to innovate by creating unique, experimental lots of coffee.

The Worka Chelbessa washing station utilizes the traditional underwater fermentation commonly used in Ethiopia, but also in 2021 experimented with dry fermentation as well at Chelbessa. This lot is a combination of both, wet and dry fermentation. In underwater fermentation the coffee is fully submerged in water for 36 to 48 hours normally, but the process can take longer. In dry fermentation the coffee is pulped and left to ferment without being underwater for 36-48 hours. After fermentation the coffee is dried for 10-14 days on raised beds.

We taste blueberry, meyer lemon, dried peach, jasmine, and black tea. We hope you try it out and enjoy!

This morning, I savored the lingering grilled peach and hibiscus aftertaste of this extremely rare Best of Yemen Al Oqabi Women Farmers - Yemenia Natural Lot #17 that we sourced from this years record-setting Best of Yemen auction. As I sip, I envision the rugged and sublime light coming off the steep 1900-2000 meter high mountains, the green coffee leaves against near sheer sand and brown colored cliffs in the distance, with streaks of light so beautiful they almost make me melancholy. 

Its no secret that many of us in coffee are obsessed with Ethiopia and the Southwestern highlands along with the Boma Plateau in South Sudan as the place where Coffea arabica evolved. Yemen is the place where coffee became a popularly consumed beverage and from where it spread first as a drink through the Muslim world. That is how the species came to be called Arabica. From there it spread as seeds to India, Java, Amsterdam, Paris, then Martinique and on to the rest of the world. 

In Yemen, Sufis first drank coffee as part of their ecstatic practices, and plantations are documented as far back as the 15th century, some believe as early as the 6th. Muslim Pilgrims coming to and from Mecca drank coffee and like any good traveler yearned to recreate the wonder of the experience at home. Thus the drink spread to places such as Aleppo, Cairo, Damascus, Istanbul, and then later on to Venice and Paris. 

Little Waves was the only US company to secure one of the 36 lots in this years record-breaking Best of Yemen auction. There were over 5,000 bids over 7 hours from 24 countries. The flavor and feeling of this coffee elicit such wonder. Its unlike anything weve ever tasted. We hope youll taste along with us.

At it's peak in 1920, Brazil was producing 80% of the world's coffee. Nowadays, the country perfectly in the bean belt (where the climate and rainfall is ideal for coffee growing) produces 1/3 of the world's coffee. 

Through the Black Producer Program, we're able to source from Black Brazilian coffee producers within the specialty coffee trade. The Peixoto family has been in the coffee industry, mostly as sharecroppers, for generations. They are among the very few Black Brazilians who own land in the Campo das Vertentes region in the south of Minas Gerais. By banding together, the Peixoto family (who are well-known and admired in their community for their strong bond) were able to purchase 44 hectares of land and plant 27,000 coffee trees. 

Sweet fruit notes peek out from behind rich chocolate and caramel flavors, adding a complexity that lets us roast this coffee a little lighter than the more traditional Brazilian coffees weve featured before. We hope you love this coffee as much as we do: the rich, vibrant history behind it and the bright future ahead

One year ago today, I planted the seeds that became these babies in a small seed-starting greenhouse over a heat mat on my kitchen counter as part of the @zhaw.coffee.excellence.center certificate in advanced studies in coffee excellence program. I was 50 years old and had never in those years not killed the few plants that I tried to grow. I think I got off to a good start because I strive to excel in my projects and this one sent me into a panic. In panic, I reached out to our friend Jose Giraldo of @cafe1959 who jumped in to help me. Over the past year Ive gone through the ups and downs of their starting and care with Joses help and Deborah Pilkington of @durhamncmastergardeners, Dr. Sebasitan Opitz Module A professor @zhaw.coffee.excellence.center, and then more recent insights from Edwin Norea @campohermoso_coffeefarms . Deborah placed two of them @sarahpdukegardens - lets call it a backup plan to be sure that some of them thrive for a long time to come!

Earlier this month, when I was talking with @coffeeliberated, it occurred to me that cultivating and caring for them has brought about a rejuvenated sense of hope in me. These plants, my babies, feel like miracles. The seeds are selected Gesha and Orange Wush Wush, which both feel so special and rare to the earth. I think of the flavors that I get to taste sometimes when I drink either of these varieties and my mind wanders to the unique microclimate in SW Ethiopia (both varieties are named after villages) where they first evolved at a high altitude under a canopy of shade among thousands of wild varieties.

When I care for these plants and experience them, in the daily quiet of watering or figuring how to help them flourish, there are moments in which they remind me of what is important in the world. Coming away for moments from the noise and horrors that are out in the world I feel the difference and need for the world to match their beauty. - Leon

We've been testing the Fellow Aiden for a while now, and the big question is: Does it brew a great cup of coffee? Short answer YES!  But, being the skeptics we are, we had to put it to the test by brewing side by side with manual pour overs. We also tried different setups: using its proprietary basket and even placing an Origami inside the Aiden.

At first, the Aiden didn't quite hit the mark. We noticed a bit of under extraction compared to our manual brews. Our guess? The bypass and flowrate were probably causing those off flavors. So, we tweaked it stretching the pouring intervals to reduce bypass and voil, it worked! We started getting seriously good cups.

In the beginning, it was tough to tell the difference between the Aiden and manual brews, but as the coffee cooled, the manually brewed cup pulled ahead. It stayed balanced even as it cooled, which we loved. So, our takeaway? Dialling in coffee for manual pourovers doesn't translate perfectly to the Aiden since you can't control the flowrate or pour intervals in the same way. 

That said, we're hoping for an update that'll let us tweak the bloom amount more than 3x and pour timing a bit more. But would we recommend it? Absolutely!

Edwin Enrique Norea

Did you know?
-Madagascar has the highest diversity of Coffea species of anywhere in the world, with a total of 65, 43 of which are threatened with extinction. 

-Durham has the most diverse population of lemurs outside of their native Madagascar and plays a role in helping safeguard them from extinction. 

-Despite the movie Madagascar, Lemurs are matrilineal, can modulate their cirdadian rhythms and sleep in a pile. Hibernating lemurs are being non-invasively observed to understand human potential for distant space travel and mouse lemurs to better understand the development of Alzheimers. Duke also reintroduces lemurs back to Madagascar as populations get separated by deforestation, to help keep them from going extinct.

-Lemurs are the most endangered mammals on Earth and every Coffea arabica variety is currently at risk of going extinct. We joined World Coffee Research as a contributing member to support their work to ensure the future of coffee. Tours are one of the ways they fund taking care of the lemurs, in addition to adopting lemurs. 

Do lemurs eat coffee? We dont know. Well have to find out.

Support @wcoffeeresearch and the @dukelemurcenter

Processing: 
cherries travel at night from Huila to Quindio to control temperature hermetically sealed bags where they begin their fermentation process.
after 24 hours, pulp the cherries, removing the skin and mucilage from the parchment.
pulped coffee in sealed tanks for an initial 24 hours of anaerobic fermentation.
Jos then washes and rinses the cherries, then
returns the mucilage free coffee parchment to dry, closed tanks for another 24 hours of fermentation.
coffee is placed on raised beds to control airflow and bring to optimal moisture content.
the coffee rests in shade for 40 days.

Second time's the charm! Our first attempt at making @aeropress iced coffee was a complete mess. But now we know that brewing at 81C is much safer  My previous try with boiling water ended in a freak accident, causing second-degree burns when the inverted AeroPress went wrong At least now we can enjoy our coffee without the risk of burns!

This time, we used one of the top recipes from @aeropress_recipe and adapted it to the upright position with a flow control filter cap, which is supposed to be safer. As @zeropuckprep emphasizes, the MOST IMPORTANT STEPS are: Step 1: Insert the paper filter, Step 2: tighten the gasket, and Step 3: double-check the gasket is tightened It made brewing with the AeroPress much safer!

We followed the 'Love me some acid' recipe, converted to the upright position:

Brewer Position: Upright
Coffee to Water Ratio: 20g coffee to 230ml water
Grind Size: Medium (@comandantegrinder MK3: 23 clicks, 1ZPresso ZP6: 3.3, 1Zpresso K Series: 7.3)
Temperature: 81C
Filter: 1 @aesirfilters or 2 classic AeroPress paper filters
Steps:

Pour 70ml of bloom water
Start the timer at 0'00 and stir for 15 seconds
At 0'15, pour up to 230ml
Steep until 1'30
At 1'30, plunge for 30 seconds
Total Brew Time: 2'00 minutes.

We used whiskey balls to rapidly cool down the coffee before transferring it to a cup with ice so that it wouldn't dilute that quickly.
